translation_notes: the two np._pubinfo.add((URIRef('http://s'), namespaces.NPX.introduces, URIRef('http://cN'))) calls become one island, `np._pubinfo += g{ <http://s> npx:introduces <http://c1>, <http://c2> }`: the repeated subject and predicate collapse into a Turtle object list, and the ten-line statement becomes one line

namespaces.NPX -> @prefix npx: <http://purl.org/nanopub/x/> . Note the trade-off: the original read the namespace IRI from the nanopub package, the ldpy version restates it literally, because @prefix produces no runtime object and cannot consume an imported Namespace
the other namespaces the test module imports (DC, RDF, DCTERMS, PROV, XSD) are unused in the region, so no prefix is declared for them (the draft declared all five)
np._pubinfo += ... rebinds the attribute to the same Graph object (Graph.__iadd__ returns self); _pubinfo is a plain attribute, unlike the read-only `pubinfo` property
the nanopub package is not installed in the evaluation venv; driver.py appends the corpus checkout to sys.path

the region returns None, so the equivalence evidence is the region's own pytest.raises: MalformedNanopubError is raised only if the pubinfo graph really ends up with two distinct npx:introduces objects on the same subject
